t:
Sec. 601. 

(a) 

For purposes of the administration of chapter 89 of title 5, United States Code, any period of enrollment under a health benefits plan administered by the Farm Credit Administration prior to the effective date of this Act shall be deemed to be a period of enrollment in a health benefits plan under chapter 89 of such title.


(b)

(1) 
An individual who, on September 30, 1995, is covered by a health benefits plan administered by the Farm Credit Administration may enroll in an approved health benefits plan described under section 8903 or 8903a of title 5, United States Code—

(A) 
either as an individual or for self and family, if such individual is an employee, annuitant, or former spouse as defined under section 8901 of such title; and


(B) 
for coverage effective on and after September 30, 1995.



(2) 
An individual who, on September 30, 1995, is entitled to continued coverage under a health benefits plan administered by the Farm Credit Administration—

(A) 
shall be deemed to be entitled to continued coverage under section 8905a of title 5, United States Code, for the same period that would have been permitted under the plan administered by the Farm Credit Administration; and


(B) 
may enroll in an approved health benefits plan described under sections 8903 or 8903a of such title in accordance with section 8905A of such title for coverage effective on and after September 30, 1995.



(3) 
An individual who, on September 30, 1995, is covered as an unmarried dependent child under a health benefits plan administered by the Farm Credit Administration and who is not a member of family as defined under section 8901(5) of title 5, United States Code—

(A) 
shall be deemed to be entitled to continued coverage under section 8905a of such title as though the individual had, on September 30, 1995, ceased to meet the requirements for being considered an unmarried dependent child under chapter 89 of such title; and


(B) 
may enroll in an approved health benefits plan described under section 8903 or 8903a of such title in accordance with section 8905a for continued coverage on and after September 30, 1995.




(c) 
The Farm Credit Administration shall transfer to the Federal Employees Health Benefits Fund established under section 8909 of title 5, United States Code, amounts determined by the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, after consultation with the Farm Credit Administration, to be necessary to reimburse the Fund for the cost of providing benefits under this section not otherwise paid for by the individuals covered by this section. The amount so transferred shall be held in the Fund and used by the Office in addition to the amounts available under section 8906(g)(1) of such title.


(d) 
The Office of Personnel Management—


(1) 
shall administer the provisions of this section to provide for—

(A) 
a period of notice and open enrollment for individuals affected by this section; and


(B) 
no lapse of health coverage for individuals who enroll in a health benefits plan under chapter 89 of title 5, United States Code, in accordance with this section; and



(2) 
may prescribe regulations to implement this section.

fable.w: The section authorizes the Office of Personnel Management to prescribe regulations, and a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation even when discretionary ("may"), because rulemaking brings the public into the decision. The tempting "No" reading rests on the fact that the consultation between OPM and the Farm Credit Administration is purely intra-federal and that the enrollment provisions concern benefits, neither of which is participation. Those points are correct but do not negate the rulemaking authority in subsection (d)(2).
fable.s: may prescribe regulations to implement this section.

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Office of Personnel Management to provide a 'period of notice and open enrollment' for individuals (employees, annuitants, etc.) affected by the transition of health benefits. This constitutes a public comment/enrollment period where outside parties (the general public/employees) participate in the decision of which health plan to select. While subsection (c) mentions consultation between federal agencies (OPM and Farm Credit Administration), which is internal, subsection (d) explicitly mandates interaction with the outside individuals regarding their enrollment choices.
qwen_block.s: (1) shall administer the provisions of this section to provide for— (A) a period of notice and open enrollment for individuals affected by this section;

opus.w: Subsection (d)(2) lets the Office of Personnel Management prescribe regulations. Under the definition and Example 6, authority to make rules counts as participation even when it is discretionary. The other features that look procedural don't count: OPM's consultation with the Farm Credit Administration is between two federal agencies, and the notice and open enrollment provisions concern enrolling in benefits, which the definition excludes.
opus.s: may prescribe regulations to implement this section.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** Two readings are tempting here, and neither holds up. First, OPM sets reimbursement amounts "after consultation with the Farm Credit Administration," but both are federal agencies, so that consultation stays inside the government. Second, the "notice and open enrollment" provisions are about enrolling in benefits, which the definition excludes. What does count is subsection (d)(2), which lets OPM prescribe regulations. Under the definition and Example 6, giving an agency rulemaking authority counts as participation, even when it is optional ("may").

qwen_chat.w: The section describes the transfer of health benefits coverage from the Farm Credit Administration to the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program. The 'consultation' mentioned is between two federal entities (OPM and FCA), which is intra-governmental. The 'open enrollment' and 'notice' periods are part of the process for individuals to apply for benefits, which the definition explicitly excludes ('It does not include applications for benefits or grants'). Therefore, there is no participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: (c) The Farm Credit Administration shall transfer to the Federal Employees Health Benefits Fund established under section 8909 of title 5, United States Code, amounts determined by the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, after consultation with the Farm Credit Administration, to be necessary to reimburse the Fund for the cost of providing benefits under this section not otherwise paid for by the individuals covered by this section.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "period of notice and open enrollment" constitutes participation because it involves individuals (outside the government) interacting with the federal system. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." Enrolling in a health benefits plan is an application for a benefit, not a consultation or coordination process where the government seeks input from outsiders to make a policy or administrative decision. The "consultation" mentioned in subsection (c) is between the Director of the Office of Personnel Management and the Farm Credit Administration, both of which are federal entities, so that is intra-governmental coordination.
